facts.fact: The Boltic article 'Best 8 Marketing Calendar Templates' was published on January 20, 2026.
The article header dates the post August 23, 2025 and lists a reading time of 23 minutes.
The article was written by Alia Soni and reviewed by Kritika Singhania.
The author says they were on a team publishing 100+ posts each month across 6 platforms, a volume they said a simple spreadsheet could not handle.
facts.quote: publishing 100+ posts each month on 6 platforms. The load could not be processed by a simple spreadsheet.

facts.fact: The article presents eight types of marketing calendar templates.
facts.quote: ## The 8 types of marketing calendar templates

facts.fact: The event marketing calendar template's key fields include follow-up actions over the three days after the event.
facts.quote: follow-up actions over the next three days

facts.fact: The editorial calendar template's suggested status field runs IDEA > DRAFT > EDITING > LIVE.
The author advises beginning marketing calendar planning 90 days or 1 month before execution.
facts.quote: You must begin planning 90 days or 1 month prior to execution.

facts.fact: The author's team was pushing out five content pieces per week, which the author says hurt quality, so the team cut output to three per week.
facts.quote: So we cut it down to three and made each one sharper, more targeted, and better aligned with our goals.

facts.fact: As an example of a sustainable pace, the author suggests planning for two high-quality blogs a month and four strong newsletters.
facts.quote: If you can create two high-quality blogs a month and send four strong newsletters, plan only for that.

facts.fact: Boltic advertises a free forever plan for organizing big data operations.
facts.quote: Organize your big data operations with a free forever plan

facts.fact: The author's calendar tracks current status using the stages Idea, In Progress, Scheduled, and Published.
facts.quote: current status (Idea, In Progress, Scheduled, Published)

facts.fact: The author plans by creating an annual roadmap, splitting it into quarterly campaigns, and then into weekly deliverables.
facts.quote: I usually create an annual roadmap and then split it into quarterly campaigns and weekly deliverables.

facts.fact: Anchor dates to lock before building a marketing calendar include product launch dates, promotion dates such as BFCM, trade shows, national holidays, and internal milestones.
facts.quote: Launch dates of the product, Primary date for promotion (such as BFCM), Trade shows or industry events, National holidays

facts.fact: The article states that a marketing plan, whether small or big, requires 4 major components to be kept ready.
facts.quote: Be it a small or a big marketing plan, these are the 4 major components that you must keep ready
